div.head: Northu 51
div.ab: Gif cyninges þegn ætsace, þonne nemne man him XII, and nime his maga XII ⁊ XII wallerwente; ⁊ gif his berste, þonne gilde he lahsliht: X healfmarc.
Gif cyninges þegn ætsace, þonne nemne man him XII, and nime his maga XII and XII wallerwente; and gif his að berste, þonne gilde he lahsliht: X healfmarc.

Wenn ein Königsthegn [das] leugnen will, dann ernenne man [das Gericht] ihm 12 [Eideshelfer], und er wähle sich von seinen Verwandten 12 und 12 [unverwandte] auserwählte Eideshelfer[?]; und wenn sein [Reinigungseid] misslingt, dann zahle er Rechtsbruchbusse: 10 Halbmark.

If a king's thegn wishes to deny [it], then let [the court] nominate 12 [oath-helpers] for him, and let him take 12 of his kinsmen and 12 [unrelated] chosen oath-helpers[?]; and if his [clearing oath] fails, then let him pay lahslit: 10 half-marks.

If a king's thegn denies it, then 12 [thegns] are to be nominated for him, and he is to take 12 of his kinsmen and 12 compurgators selected for him [?]; and if his [oath] fails, he is then to pay lahslit: 10 half-marks.

If a king’s thane denies the charge, then twelve are to be chosen for him, and he is to select twelve kinsmen and twelve neutral witnesses; and if his oath fails then he is to pay lahslit: ten half-marks.

note.label: same pool of ideas
note.quote: after II Cn 12 – 15:1a on payment of 'lahslit' came clauses drawing on the same pool of ideas as Northu. 51 - 53

div.note: ‘wallerwente’ is corrupt, Liebermann thinks, from Norse ‘valinvitni’ (chosen witnesses). After ‘his’ supply ‘að’ (which D also skips elsewhere) or ‘lad’, or read ‘him þæt’ as in 52; Thorpe alters to ‘hit’. Clauses 51–53 are used in the Instituta Cnuti II 15.1.; W: corrected against Rabin p. 311, October 2026 (was “If a king’s thane denies the charge, then twelve are to be chosen for him, and he is to select twelve kinsmen and twelve neutral witnesses; and if his oath fails then he is to pay lahslit: ten half-marks.”, now “If a king’s thane denies the charge, then twelve are to be chosen for him, and he is to select twelve kinsmen and twelve neutral witnesses; and if his oath fails then he is to pay lahslit: ten half-marks. (expanded letters in italics: lahslit)”)

Verderbt aus Nord. valinvitni? [Den Hinweis auf Nord. Recht verdanke ich K. v. Maurer. A. Heusler bemerkt freundlich, ein Skandinavien fehlendes *valinvitni erkläre sich vielleicht als lokale Kurzform zu valinkunn vitni.]

Corrupted from Norse valinvitni? [I owe the reference to Norse law to K. v. Maurer. A. Heusler kindly remarks that a *valinvitni, not found in Scandinavia, may perhaps be explained as a local short form of valinkunn vitni.]
Ergänze að (was D auch o. S. 245² überspringt) oder lad oder bessere nach 52 hī ꝥ; Thorpe ändert hit.
Supply að (which D also skips above, p. 245²) or lad, or correct after 52 to hī ꝥ; Thorpe alters to hit.

Vgl. Gl Auswahleid 11. 16 über teils ernannte, teils vom Schwörer erwählte Helfer. Deren Zahl 36 ebd. Eideshelfer 9. 44f. Vermutlich sind wie 52f. Standesgenossen des Hauptschwörers, hier also Königsthegnas gemeint; sonst würde man men erwarten

Cf. Gl Auswahleid 11. 16 on helpers partly nominated and partly chosen by the swearer. On their number, 36, ibid. Eideshelfer 9. 44f. Presumably, as in 52f., peers of the principal swearer, here therefore king’s thegns, are meant; otherwise one would expect men

Die Erklärung Früherer aus einem Völkernamen, Kelten und bes. Gwent, ist allgemein aufgegeben.—Mit dem Nord. Rechtsausdruck valinkunnr, der im Norden ebenfalls in der blutsverwandte Helfer ausschliessenden Eideshilfe (Fritz Gesetzl. Verwandt. in Savigny Zs. RG., Germ. 36, 270) vorkommt, verbinden das Wort Steenstrup Danelag 238, Maurer (freundl. Mitt. 12. Aug. 1899), Amira, Heusler (29. XI. 1901). E. Hertzberg im Arkiv for Nord. Filol. V (1889) 353 und Norges gamle love V 2 (1895), Gloss. 683 erklärt valinkunnr: ‘unverwandt, den streitenden Parteien nicht nah verbundenes Geschlecht’. [Das Erfordernis der Nichtverwandtschaft wurde im späteren Breve Venire facias an die Jury gestellt; Athenæum Apr. 1902 p. 423.] Das Wort besteht aus valin (pt. pf. von velja wählen, dessen Entsprechung wale ‘wählen, Wahl’ mengl. und heute nordengl. lautet) und kunnr ‘verwandt’ und bed. ursprünglich ‘aus erwähltem (im Ggs. zum eigenen) Geschlecht’. Da der Hauptschwörer gern angesehene Eideshelfer sich wählte, erhielt das Wort die Bed. ‘unverwandt’ und ‘angesehenen Geschlechts’. [Da nun vendr, meint Maurer, ‘verwandt’ bedeuten kann, so könne *valinvend für valinkunnr stehen. Er selbst kann wente in 52. 53 dann nur für ‘unverständige Abkürzung’ erklären: letzteres scheint mir unmöglich.]—Nord. vitni ist Collectivum nt. sg. ‘Eideshelferschaft’.—Zu der von mir angenommenen Verschreibung des n zu r vgl. Wb 152 Z. 17; 180 Sp. 1 Z. 8 v. u. [Nicht zu erklären ist wallerwente etwa als ‘Landhufen der Wallerhalter (Festungsbürger)’, auf die Synonymität hin von weall(ge)weorc mit burhbot, wegen der Bed. went ‘Flächenmass von Grund und Boden’, und aus Analogie mit den murales mansiones, die murum reficient im Domesday I 154.]

The explanation by earlier scholars from the name of a people, the Celts and esp. Gwent, has been generally abandoned.—The word is connected with the Norse legal term valinkunnr, which in the North likewise occurs in the kind of oath-help that excludes helpers related by blood (Fritz Gesetzl. Verwandt. in Savigny Zs. RG., Germ. 36, 270), by Steenstrup Danelag 238, Maurer (kind communication of 12 Aug. 1899), Amira and Heusler (29. XI. 1901). E. Hertzberg in the Arkiv for Nord. Filol. V (1889) 353 and Norges gamle love V 2 (1895), Gloss. 683 explains valinkunnr as ‘unrelated, of a family not closely connected with the litigating parties’. [The requirement of non-kinship was made of the jury in the later writ Venire facias; Athenæum Apr. 1902 p. 423.] The word consists of valin (past part. of velja ‘choose’, whose equivalent is wale ‘choose, choice’ in Middle English and in Northern English today) and kunnr ‘related’, and originally meant ‘of a chosen kin (as opposed to one’s own)’. Since the principal swearer liked to choose respected oath-helpers, the word acquired the meanings ‘unrelated’ and ‘of respected family’. [Since vendr, Maurer thinks, can mean ‘related’, *valinvend could stand for valinkunnr. He himself can then explain wente in 52. 53 only as an ‘unintelligent abbreviation’: the latter seems to me impossible.]—Norse vitni is a collective neut. sg. ‘body of oath-helpers’.—On the miswriting of n as r which I assume, cf. Wb 152 l. 17; 180 col. 1 l. 8 from bottom. [wallerwente is not to be explained as, say, ‘hides of the wall-keepers (inhabitants of a fortress)’, on the strength of the synonymy of weall(ge)weorc with burhbot, because of the meaning of went ‘a measure of area of land’, and by analogy with the murales mansiones which murum reficient in Domesday I 154.]

The meaning of the term wallerwente is reasonably clear, though its form has not been fully explained. Liebermann suggests that it is a corruption of Old Norse valinvitni “chosen (unrelated) witness”.
